primitives.name: Red Eligibility State Monitor

primitives.assumptions: Performance stats are inactive during red eligibility.

layer2.mapping: GSE operational mode shifts to conservative monitoring when GSI eligibility state is red.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through a temporal cron-based signal generation pipeline that aggregates predictive models from Kalshi, FPI, ClubElo, Poisson, and Elo. The system's integrity is maintained by ensuring that the signal board only activates when the slate is fresh—defined as having been recently published. This prevents stale odds from influencing decisions, aligning with a Bayesian framework where posterior beliefs are updated only upon valid evidence. The red eligibility state disables performance statistics when model calibration metrics (Brier, ECE, RES) fall below acceptable thresholds, enforcing a conservative operational mode. The kill switch ensures that even if models produce signals, they are not exposed unless the slate meets freshness criteria. This architecture embodies a dual-layered robustness: one against data staleness and another against model misalignment. Failure modes include cron misfires, stale data ingestion, or incorrect freshness thresholds leading to either false positives or negatives in signal exposure.
